attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'basically', the media and market actors, and the GPU-buyer scope. The evaluative words 'captured' and 'brainless' are rightly left unscored.

contract.note: The plain reading (a pervasive pattern, exceptions allowed, 2023–2025 taken from the surrounding examples) is ordinary and fair. Requiring a representative sample suits a claim about a broad pattern.

evidence.note: Analyst preview from July 2024 that separates AI's 7-point share of Azure growth from total growth. It is one counterexample to indiscriminate attribution and cannot show prevalence.
Coverage of Amazon's October 2024 results credits cloud and advertising, not AI wholesale. It is a single counterexample to the claimed pattern, not a measure of how common the pattern was.
CNBC links AI to extra cloud business, but as Amazon's own assertion. It does not show that AI got credit for essentially all growth.

reviews.rationale: Two items separate AI from other growth drivers, but the contract says isolated counterexamples cannot disprove a pattern qualified by 'basically'. The packet has no representative sample of coverage or investor commentary, so neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post. 'I believe' introduces his position.

semantics.note: Correctly a causal claim. Merging 'NVIDIA/AI bubble' slightly blurs his split: inflating the NVIDIA bubble versus rationalizing the AI bubble. Reputational laundering is dropped but kept in the contract as a mechanism. 'I believe' is not one of the listed hedges.

contract.note: Reading 'critical' as a major but not sole contribution is fair. Requiring causal separation from fundamentals is appropriate for a causal claim.

evidence.note: A September 2023 article frames the Bernstein defence favourably. It shows amplification happened once but shows no causal effect on valuation or investment.
A 2026 study finds speculative episodes across semiconductor stocks. It does not measure what analysts or the media contributed to them.
The same study finds no bubble at Apple, Microsoft or Amazon. That qualifies the wider bubble premise but says nothing about analyst or media causation.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet separates an analyst or media effect from earnings, demand or financing conditions, and nothing shows the claimed promotion had no substantial effect. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. The Semafor paraphrase comes after it and is separate.

semantics.note: 'Is not coming back' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The resignation is a historical premise.

contract.note: It is fair to count only an actual return to a CEO-level role as contradiction. With no deadline, support needs an irreversible event. That is reasonable.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 8-K from 12 November 2026 confirms the resignation and the interim CEO, which is the premise. A successor search does not rule out a return.
CNBC on 16 November 2026: an anonymous source says the board is not considering a return, while others call for reinstatement. That is about current intentions, not a decisive event.

reviews.rationale: The resignation is confirmed. Huang has not returned as of the evaluation date, and no irreversible event bars a return. The forecast has no deadline and no conclusive event has occurred, so it cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the three mechanisms named in context and the 'sustain and amplify' claim.

contract.note: Reading 'amplified' as spending beyond what would otherwise have happened is ordinary. Whether 'industry-wide' needs a measured aggregate effect or only a broad causal contribution is a choice the speaker did not make, and it drives the result.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own July 2026 disclosure describes a credit-support model meant to help AI clouds buy infrastructure. It shows a mechanism, not realized extra spending.
The January 2026 joint filing records a $2B equity investment and plans to use NVIDIA's balance sheet to speed CoreWeave's buildout. It does not establish the counterfactual extra spending.

reviews.rationale: Company disclosures show NVIDIA's investments and credit-support mechanisms. None measures spending that would not otherwise have happened, or an industry-wide effect. No evidence shows the interventions merely replaced other funding, so neither condition is met.
